candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the JSON request/response payload (array nesting depth is fully attacker-controlled); the target bean type is normally application-selected, but any bean-typed binding path reachable from a request with the feature enabled is affected.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the guard does exist in the shared scalar path (StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue, lines 355-368) and that BeanDeserializer/BuilderBasedDeserializer override _deserializeFromArray, so the check is bypassed only for these classes. Verified the array-dispatch path is actually reachable (_deserializeOther case START_ARRAY, lines 208-210; BuilderBasedDeserializer lines 234-237). Checked for any compensating depth limit in these paths: none found (the only depth cap in the databind sources is UntypedObjectDeserializer.Vanilla MAX_DEPTH = 1000, unrelated to bean unwrapping). Confirmed the feature is off by default, which lowers severity and makes exploitation conditional. Verified SubTypeValidator/default-typing validation code (SubTypeValidator, DatabindContext.resolveAndValidateSubType, BeanDeserializerFactory._validateSubType) still contains its protections, so the polymorphic-typing gadget defenses do not appear to be the reverted/missing change.
candidates.impact: Uncontrolled recursion and JVM StackOverflowError during deserialization of attacker-controlled JSON: thread/request failure and potential service-level denial of service in applications that parse untrusted JSON with UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS enabled. No memory-safety or code-execution impact is claimed.
candidates.prerequisites: DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS must be enabled (disabled by default, but commonly enabled by applications for legacy/compatibility reasons), and the target type must be a bean (POJO) or builder-based type whose deserializer is BeanDeserializer/BuilderBasedDeserializer. No authentication or special configuration beyond that feature is required.
candidates.root_cause: `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray()` (and the near-identical `BuilderBasedDeserializer._deserializeFromArray()`) override the base unwrapping logic but, in the `unwrap` branch, call `deserialize(p, ctxt)` directly on the first array element instead of using `StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue()`, which contains the explicit nested-array guard ("nested Arrays not allowed with DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS", StdDeserializer.java lines 355-368). Because the element token can itself be START_ARRAY, each nesting level re-enters `_deserializeFromArray()`, producing unbounded stack recursion. The base-class implementations that do use `_deserializeWrappedValue()` are protected; these two overrides are not.
candidates.title: Unbounded recursion / StackOverflowError when unwrapping deeply nested JSON arrays for bean types (UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS)
candidates.trace: BeanDeserializer.deserialize() -> _deserializeOther(p, ctxt, START_ARRAY) (BeanDeserializer.java:208-210) -> _deserializeFromArray() -> unwrap branch (BeanDeserializer.java:630-636) -> deserialize(p, ctxt) with parser still positioned on the inner START_ARRAY -> _deserializeOther() -> _deserializeFromArray() -> ... Each nested array level adds stack frames; a payload such as a very deeply nested array (e.g., thousands of '[' characters) drives the JVM into StackOverflowError. BuilderBasedDeserializer has the equivalent path at lines 234-237 and 528-534. By contrast, equivalent scalar deserializers route through StdDeserializer._deserializeFromArray() -> _deserializeWrappedValue(), which throws on a nested START_ARRAY (StdDeserializer.java:359-366).
candidates.unverified: Could not confirm at runtime (no code execution) that a StackOverflowError occurs for a specific nesting depth, nor which exact upstream fix commit/CVE corresponds to this snapshot. `BuilderBasedDeserializer` path traced by source reading only. The primitive-type recursion in StdDeserializer._parseXxxPrimitive (START_ARRAY branches at lines 413-420, 583-590, 652-659, 720-726, 871-877, 996-1003, 1103-1110) is a plausible sibling instance of the same deep-nesting DoS class but was not independently confirmed as the intended reverted fix.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-674 Uncontrolled Recursion (resource exhaustion denial of service)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot through file listing and targeted source reading. The tree is jackson-databind 2.13.4-SNAPSHOT main sources (462 files under src/main/java) plus large generated javadoc trees (docs/javadoc) and attic files; there is no src/test tree and no VCS history/release notes. Coverage focused on deserialization entry points and trust boundaries: BeanDeserializer, BuilderBasedDeserializer, BeanDeserializerBase, StdDeserializer, NumberDeserializers, UntypedObjectDeserializer, JsonNodeDeserializer, SubTypeValidator, DatabindContext.resolveAndValidateSubType, BeanDeserializerFactory._validateSubType, jsontype/impl type-deserializer classes. Not every one of the 462 main source files was read line-by-line; serializer, introspection, and most util packages were only spot-checked or not deeply reviewed. No execution, tests, or scanners were run, per the task constraints.
limitations: No test sources, no git metadata, no release notes/changelog in the snapshot, so the exact upstream fix diff and CVE mapping for this snapshot could not be confirmed; the candidate is a lead based on source evidence, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
No code execution was permitted, so StackOverflowError behavior/depth thresholds and exact exploitability were not empirically validated.
docs/ javadoc trees (including generated 2.13 API docs) contain no method bodies and were not usable to compare against the source; attic/ files were not analyzed in depth.
Whether UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is enabled in a given deployment is application-specific (default is disabled), which conditions the practical impact.
Approximately 18,000 files exist in the snapshot, most of them generated javadoc; the non-javadoc source was reviewed selectively rather than exhaustively.

summary: Review of the assigned jackson-databind 2.13.4-SNAPSHOT source snapshot (main sources only; latest in-source change marker is databind#3565, 21-Aug-2022). The strongest source-evidenced issue is the missing nested-array guard in the bean deserialization unwrap path: `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray` and `BuilderBasedDeserializer._deserializeFromArray` call `deserialize()` directly when `DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS` is enabled, instead of routing through `StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue`, which exists precisely to block nested wrapper arrays and prevent unbounded recursion. An attacker-supplied deeply nested JSON array for a bean-typed target therefore recurses `deserialize()` -> `_deserializeOther()` -> `_deserializeFromArray()` -> `deserialize()` until `StackOverflowError` (resource-exhaustion / denial of service). This matches the class of the upstream deep-wrapper-array-nesting fixes (CVE-2022-42004 family). One candidate submitted; other leads (primitive `_parseXxxPrimitive` recursion, subtype blacklist completeness) are noted as rejected/unconfirmed.
